additional_info.subject: ID0482405/DC/Si-D/IT-[Y2/T3314176150001] Log check CRM:02681001552
additional_info.body:
Dear Maria,
Thank you for contacting eMobility Support.
Following your report, and after checking the charging session, we see in the logs that the charger was having trouble connecting to the network.
When the charger has no connection, it is not possible to end a charging session, as the charger cannot follow the commands given.
Here you are able to see in the logs that the communication between the car and the charger lost.
The charger looks healthy, we only see that the dc1 is not operative, but this has been put unavailable from the client side.
No further errorflags are showing.
We hope this has informed you enough.
We will keep an eye on the charger for the next 24 hours to see if any further errors will show.
Thank you.
Kind regards,
Priscilla van Wettum

additional_info.subject: Log check
additional_info.body:
Please note that we have checked multiple charging sessions, from what we received from the client.
The only issues we have seen during the charging sessions are related to the network, and to the EV side. The charging sessions are charging, and stopping until the EV is not requesting anymore kw from the charger.
The RFID issues you are mentioning, are related to the backend system of the client. This is also the case for the errors the client is receiving in their backend system saying the following.
I suggest you to check the network connection of the charger, including the internet cable, and the router.
In the following you can see that the charger had trouble connecting to the network, and then received a request from the backend to stop the charging session. This is all related to the backend of the client.
I hope to have informed you enough.
Kind regards,
Priscilla van Wettum

additional_info.subject: RE: R: ID0482405/DC/Si-D/IT-[Y2/T3314176150001] Log check CRM:03209000298
additional_info.body:
Dear recipient,
Today, we conducted an on-site analysis of the charger. After reviewing the logs related to the reported charging sessions, we identified an error on the DC2 side. During the parameter discovery step, the charger was unable to receive the cable check signal from the vehicle. This issue was caused by a mask on the plug that was not properly closed, and our Ecog component, which manages the connection with the vehicle, was not functioning correctly.
After tightening the plug and replacing the faulty component, we conducted several charging sessions without any errors.
We can now proceed with closing this ticket.
Thank you for your patience.
Best regards,
CANCELLIERI, Giuseppe (SI E EU IT)
Please find the related report attached
